thread:
maria_support: Quick heads-up — scheduling a wave-based cutover for the new rate policy tomorrow 09:00 PT. Target is reducing default per-account per-minute from 600 -> 400 and tightening long-tail quotas. Doc: https://redwood.internal/releases/wave-ratepolicy (internal). Need SRE + Support on standby for 09:00-11:00 PT. :eyes:
liam_engrel: Thanks. Can you paste the exact rollout plan/steps here? Is this a canary or full wave?
maria_support: Wave rollout: 1) push config to 5% of traffic for 20m, 2) expand to 25% for 30m, 3) expand to 60% for 30m, 4) full. If any 5xx/429 spike or error budget breach -> abort and rollback. Metric gates in Grafana: 429 rate, p50/p95 latency, auth failures, error budget (SLOs).
anya_sre: I'll own the metric gates and real-time checks. Which dashboards & queries? Share links and thresholds.
liam_engrel: Gate thresholds: 429 > 0.5% sustained over 5m OR p95 latency increase > 30% over baseline OR auth_fails > 0.2% -> pause. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/rl/ratepolicy-waves (internal). I also pushed alerts to the release channel.
sam_supportlead: Support standby plan: we'll monitor incoming escalations, enable rapid escalation to eng-releases if customers report 429s. Pre-created mitigation playbook: short-term per-customer quota bump, token grace increase, or rolling back the policy. I'll keep the support hotline open.
maria_support: Adding the rollback command here for quick access — use only on explicit SRE+Release lead approval:
```bash
# rollback to previous policy version
releasectl rollback --policy wave-2026-03 --to v1
# OR toggle safe-fallback to preserve old limits immediately
releasectl toggle feature-ratepolicy-fallback --on
```
liam_engrel: On the subject of rollback, can we do a targeted rollback for affected tenant(s) instead of global? Some customers should not be impacted.
anya_sre: Yes — the runtime supports tenant-scoped overrides. Command to patch tenant quota:
```bash
# set tenant override (5m window)
apictl tenants patch --id tenant-acme --rate-limit-per-minute 800 --reason "emergency override"
```
maria_support: Repro snippet for a customer who already hit issues in staging — if you see this, it's quota exhaustion (429) not auth:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"test"}'
# response headers of interest: X-RW-RateLimit-Limit, X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After, X-RW-Quota-Window
```
liam_engrel: Good. Also watch billing spikes — last trial cohort consumed tokens faster than predicted and exhausted quotas unexpectedly. If billing pipeline triggers quota enforcement, that'll cause sudden 429s. Support: check recent invoice/usage spikes for affected tenants.
sam_supportlead: Will do. I'll assign two people to watch billing dashboards and a third to triage any incoming tickets.
anya_sre: Deploy-bot prepping the rollout now in dry-run mode. Please stand by and report any anomalies. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: releasectl: dry-run successful for wave-2026-03; canary config validated. Rolling windows and histogram targets set.
maria_support: Final sync at 08:45 PT in #eng-releases. If we see any sign of unexpected 5xx/latency regressions during 5% canary, we abort and rollback. Assigning on-call: @anya_sre lead, @liam_engrel backup, support lead @sam_supportlead.
liam_engrel: I'll be on Zoom and watching traces (Link: https://traces.redwood/trace?q=ratepolicy). If anything odd, I'll cut the canary immediately and open a postmortem thread.
sam_supportlead: Copy — support pinned playbook and tenant override commands in the support docs. I'll post a short customer-facing note template if we need to communicate an outage.
maria_support: Great. If nobody objects, proceeding with the plan. Otherwise raise now. :white_check_mark:
